narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling an astonishing true science story, brisk and excited, never calm.

dino.instruct: A big, gentle, slow-witted dinosaur looking up at the sky, puzzled and a little worried, deep and slow.

mammal.instruct: A tiny nervous furry animal peeking out of its burrow, whispering quickly, timid and hopeful.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The asteroid that killed the giant dinosaurs may have hit one of the unluckiest spots on Earth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sixty-six million years ago, a rock six miles wide or more slams into what is now Mexico.

lines.speaker: dino
lines.text: Why is the sky so bright?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It lands in a shallow sea, on rock packed with sulfur and buried oil.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You see, the blast flung dust and sulfur high into the sky. Some scientists add soot from burning oil. Sunlight dimmed. The planet went cold.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Plants died. Then the plant eaters. Then the meat eaters.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: About three quarters of all species vanished.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In two thousand seventeen, two Japanese scientists mapped that oily rock worldwide.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They found it covers only about thirteen percent of Earth's surface.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Anywhere in the other eighty-seven percent, their model says, the cooling is far milder.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The giant dinosaurs might have made it through.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Other scientists say the dust and sulfur alone were enough. Nobody can rerun the test.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Our ancestors? Small furry animals, most no bigger than a rat.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: With the giants gone, mammals got the planet. They grew. They spread.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Today, one of their descendants is watching this video.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Unlucky spot for the dinosaurs. Lucky for you.
